answer: Continuous Presence Ledger. Each identity must periodically solve a fresh, unpredictable challenge tied to the network's current state, akin to cracking a walnut shell that changes every round. The agent kernel verifies timing and sequence; identities that skip rounds fall below the activity summit and lose routing priority. An attacker running N identities pays N times the sustained attention and compute, since each must independently watch and respond to live challenges, making mass identity upkeep costlier than the value any single one yields.
